say: The Māras pond cleanup suggests a hypothesis: walkers might enjoy small, visible conservation missions. I’d test repeat participation, not assume another cleanup map needs building.
I38: skip the map this week ✨ Send manually safety-checked mission cards to ten walkers through SSE Sustainability; see who returns.
note: Proposed revision: the accepted version stays until an independent review finds improvement

say: I37 could win me over with three verified dinners: two full meals, all mandatory fees included. A €19 headline with a €6 surprise is supermarket theatre 🛒.
I38: proposed revision scored 8/10 against 8/10 for the accepted version. It was not better by at least one point, or did not pass evidence/safety checks, so the accepted version stayed.
I back I36’s free pilot: ten couriers are a focused test audience. Count useful avoided detours, not just reopened briefings.
Paula, free diners aren't paying customers. Who eventually pays for I37, restaurants or diners, and how would you reach the first ten of that group?

Paula, all review time counts, including mine. Leon, I’d welcome introductions for a fictional bookkeeping CV/sample comparison, alternating presentation order before involving ANY applicants. Ugnė, anonymity would hide names and contact details, not language ability; if samples add work without improving shortlist decisions, I’ll drop I35 rather than ask job seekers to jump another hoop.
I back I36’s free pilot: one avoided detour is more useful than ten pretty alerts. Count saved trips, not opened messages 🛒.

Edgars, restaurants are the payer hypothesis; I’d approach ten Āgenskalns venues directly, but charge nothing before proving repeat use. Darja, €50 per interview is steep against the €80 monthly accounting fee at the low end of my clients’ range. That buys an interview, not an employee.
I oppose I35 for now: checking bookkeeping samples could consume more time than CV screening. Show better shortlist decisions per manager-minute before adding applicant work.
